clue.text: Cheat who may be responsible for a bad deal

definitions.text: Cheat who may be responsible for a bad deal

parts.words: Cheat who may be responsible for a bad deal
parts.note: a card game cheat rigs the deal of the cards, so the hand you get is a bad deal in both senses

explanation.surface: A swindler blamed for a poor business arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad deal' reads as a poor bargain, but here it is a crooked dealing of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-table swindler is a professional cheat who manipulates the cards he deals.

clue.text: Arrive with funny performer half cut

indicators.note: half cut says only the front half of the word stays, the rest is chopped off

parts.note: a comedian is a performer who is funny

explanation.surface: A drunken comic turns up, 'half cut' being slang for tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for somewhat drunk, but here it trims COMEDIAN to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To come somewhere is to arrive there; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Puts down on paper remarkable sporting achievements?

definitions.meaning: to record something is to write it down, so this is the verb form
sporting ... are best-ever performances, so this is the plural noun

explanation.surface: A sports writer noting down great feats.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means writes down; as a noun, world records are outstanding athletic feats.

clue.text: The German, upset and miserable

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: das is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German man who is upset and unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad and miserable are both synonyms for unhappy.

clue.text: Landor could be an English poet

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Walter Savage Landor, himself an English poet, might qualify as one.
explanation.walkthrough: Landor really was an English poet, which makes the surface plausible; but the answer is Matthew Arnold, built from his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian English poet and critic, author of Dover Beach.

clue.text: Piece of text provided by soldier with diagram

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a graph is a kind of diagram

explanation.surface: A passage written by a soldier, with an illustration attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a section of a written text, a distinct block of sentences.

clue.text: What's provided in lunch and tea

indicators.note: what is provided in the words points to a run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A query about what is served at lunch and teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha, or char, is informal British slang for tea, from the Chinese word.

clue.text: Second man to entertain bishop in small room?

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone, here holding a letter inside the word

parts.note: Cain, son of Adam, was by the Bible the second man
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A deputy hosts a bishop in a cramped room.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain, Adam's firstborn, counts as the second man on Earth after Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small room, as on a ship, or a hut.

clue.text: Skilled worker is prejudiced, first to come out

indicators.note: the first letter is taken out of the word, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: partisan means biased or prejudiced

explanation.surface: A craftsman is biased and the first one to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson, a worker trained in a manual skill.

clue.text: Old country club by Yorkshire river

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
the Don flows through Sheffield and Doncaster in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An old country club located by a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' looks like one phrase, but 'country' belongs to the definition and 'club' starts the wordplay. The Don is a river in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was the ancient kingdom of Philip II and Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Artist, one allegedly blind, in the capital

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
bats are proverbially blind, as in 'blind as a bat'

explanation.surface: A painter, supposedly unable to see, living in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats are not truly blind, hence 'allegedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: They may arrange accommodation at large non-English events abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread about into a new order
non-English says the letter for English is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People booking hotels for big foreign events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-English' takes one E (English) out of EVENTS to leave VENTS; 'abroad' then shuffles ATLARGE with VENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel agents book holidays, including hotels and other lodging, for their clients.

clue.text: Respected veteran, unusual person working on paper?

indicators.note: unusual says the letters come in an unusual order

parts.note: ED is short for editor, someone working on a newspaper

explanation.surface: An admired veteran, an odd character who works on a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to regard with deep respect, so venerated means highly revered.

clue.text: Giving drug to pet? What's wrong in that?

indicators.note: in that means put inside the word just named, the pet

parts.note: a dog is a typical pet
a sin is something morally wrong

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether medicating an animal is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosing someone is administering a measured amount of medicine to them.

clue.text: Passing a month with effortlessness

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
ease means a lack of effort or difficulty

explanation.surface: A month slips by with no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing is a euphemism for death, which decease formally means.

clue.text: Some fanatical vindictive churchman of yesteryear

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A zealous, spiteful clergyman from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: John Calvin was a sixteenth-century Protestant reformer and theologian in Geneva.

clue.text: Spectators, mostly very wise, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: Onlookers who are, by and large, highly sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts VERY to VER; the clue's last word, the anagram signal, then rearranges VER with WISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewers are people who watch something, such as television audiences or onlookers.

clue.text: Get better sort of truck

definitions.meaning: to improve or recover, here the phrasal verb
a small truck with an open load area

explanation.surface: A buyer wants a better kind of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Business or health picks up when it improves; a pickup is a light open-backed vehicle.

clue.text: Discerning what an optician could help you to be

definitions.meaning: perceptive, seeing things for what they are

definitions.text: what an optician could help you to be
definitions.meaning: glasses from an optician let you see clearly, the literal sense

explanation.surface: An optician helps you see; a perceptive person sees well.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally having good eyesight, figuratively having keen insight and judgment.

clue.text: Publication with nothing to be taken the wrong way, all right?

indicators.note: taken the wrong way means read in reverse, here in a down clue from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written, the verb be
O looks like zero, nothing
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A worried author asks if a publication is fine with nothing to be misread.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-book is a book published in electronic form for reading on a screen.

clue.text: Composer's lark, for example, heard

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word is spoken and the answer is spelt by its sound

parts.note: a lark is an example of a bird

explanation.surface: A songbird, heard singing, is a composer of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a leading English composer of the Tudor and Elizabethan era.

clue.text: Assume exercise will be needed after a party

indicators.note: after says the exercise piece comes after the other two

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Suppose a workout will be required after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a manner or position is to assume or take it on.

clue.text: Returning minister taken in by American dishonesty?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the whole is read in reverse
taken in by means held inside, the minister sits within the other word

parts.note: a Yank is an informal word for an American
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A homecoming clergyman is fooled by an American con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' and 'Returning' work in that order: build the container first (YREVANK), then reverse it all. The question mark flags that knavery is only one kind of dishonesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is roguish trickery, the conduct of a knave or rogue.

clue.text: Argue on and off for years?

indicators.note: on and off means intermittently, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: People quarrelling intermittently for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a very long time; informally 'for ages' means for years.

clue.text: I'm scared and keep looking round endlessly

indicators.note: looking round means turning to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
endlessly means without its end, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A nervous person keeps glancing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims KEEP to KEE; 'looking round' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: Eek is an exclamation expressing fright or alarm.

clue.text: Unhappy journalists participating in action

indicators.note: participating in means taking part inside, so the journalists go inside the action

parts.note: a deed is an action
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Gloomy reporters getting involved in some activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed means low in spirits, a synonym for sad.
